methods.label: Apply the angle bisector theorem twice
methods.explanation:
Use the standard notation \(a=BC\), \(b=CA\), and \(c=AB\). The angle bisector theorem relates each divided side to the two sides adjacent to the bisected angle.

Since \(CM\) bisects angle \(C\),
\[
\frac{AM}{MB}=\frac{CA}{CB}=\frac ba.
\]
Since \(AL\) bisects angle \(A\),
\[
\frac{BL}{LC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac cb,
\qquad
\frac{CL}{LB}=\frac bc.
\]
All these lengths are positive, so we may divide the two ratios. The required multiplier is
\[
k=\frac{AM/MB}{CL/LB}
=\frac{b/a}{b/c}
=\frac ca.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\dfrac ca\), choice E.
